heading: Application for Graduate Legal Technology Analyst
paragraphs: I am applying for the Graduate Legal Technology Analyst scheme in Birmingham because it sits exactly where my interests meet: technology applied to a professional service, in a sector being reshaped by AI and automation. What draws me to your programme specifically is its structure - nine months in the Technology Products team learning how the firm's technology estate is shaped and delivered, then twelve months embedded in a Practice Group seeing whether that technology actually works for the lawyers and clients using it. That is the full loop, and it is the part of legal technology I most want to understand.

My MSc in Information Security at Royal Holloway, awarded with Merit, included Secure Business Architectures and Security Management alongside digital forensics and network security, and I hold CompTIA Security+ and ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity. My training is in asking how a system is supposed to work, finding where it actually does not, and setting out what would fix it - which is the same discipline behind analysing a business process and translating it into a practical solution. I also understand the obligations that come with handling other people's information: data protection, access control and evidence are central to everything I have studied, and they matter more, not less, in legal services.

Gathering requirements from busy people is already most of what I do. As an IT Support Assistant I handle four to five access requests a day through on-premises Active Directory: I take a business request, confirm the approval behind it, work out precisely what the person needs, grant only that with a recorded expiry, and document the decision - the same translation from a stakeholder's need into a controlled technical change. At Co-op, as Person in Charge, I run weekly risk assessments and daily compliance checks against operational controls while coordinating seven or eight colleagues, which means explaining requirements to people who would rather be doing their own job. That is stakeholder engagement in practice, and it is where I learned that a solution nobody adopts is not a solution.

I also test and document what I build. I developed a detection browser extension with twenty-five patterns and ran over 150 manual test cases to 93.7% accuracy, deliberately checking for false positives because a tool that flags the wrong thing costs more time than it saves. I built a phishing-analysis prototype in Python with the Gmail API and an LLM that maps findings to MITRE ATT&CK and keeps every result for a human to validate before anything is acted on - a habit that matters more as AI tools move into professional work. My wider toolkit is Python, PowerShell, SQL and API integration. For a product delivery team, the value is someone who writes down what was agreed, tests whether it works, and reports the result honestly, including when it does not.

I am curious about emerging technology rather than intimidated by it, I am comfortable being the person who asks the obvious question, and I am committed to the twenty-one months it takes to build real depth of knowledge in this field. I am based in London and would relocate for the Birmingham office. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how I could contribute to your Legal Technology teams.
